newsitem.title: UK: Siebe shares drop after APV bid.
newsitem.headline: Siebe shares drop after APV bid.

text.p: Shares in Siebe Plc dropped in pre-market trading on Friday after the control systems maker announced a 327.4 million stg bid for process engineering group APV Plc.
The stock was down 21p at 937-1/2 by 0723 GMT, not far from its eight-month low of 889p set on April 29. APV was up 13p at 102-1/2.
Analysts said the acquisiton looked a good fit, with Siebe's existing businesses but the price it was paying could be hard to justify.

"The industrial logic is fairly sound," said Chris Hemingway, analyst at Lehman Brothers, "the the way Siebe has been developing meant the food industry has become a big new potential market and APV was already a competitor."
Yet Hemingway pointed out that the acquisition price was a hefty twenty times APV's historic earnings and some 2.75 times the book value of its assets.

"It is a very expensive purchase," the Lehman analyst said, "they will have to double the profits of the business before it adds anything in terms of shareholder value...the fact that adds to earnings per share is irrelevant."
Siebe said the acquisition will position it as the leading global supplier of control systems to the food, beverage and pharmaceutical industries.
It said the takeover would "unlock significant growth potential" for APV with the introduction of Siebe's Foxboro Intelligent Automation System into APV's product range.
